biography.plain_text: Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Al Saud was crown prince of Saudi Arabia from 2005 until his death in 2011. A son of founding king Abdulaziz, he had led the defence and aviation ministry since 1962, after earlier service as Riyadh governor and as agriculture and communications minister. His public career spanned six decades.

long_biography.plain_text:
Prince Sultan's most durable civilian legacy grew from the charitable foundation he established in Riyadh in 1995. Its projects included Sultan bin Abdulaziz Humanitarian City, social housing and medical and educational programmes. Scientific research and support for people with disabilities helped turn personal patronage into institutions designed to continue beyond his lifetime.

He also sponsored specialist programmes linking universities and public needs, from medical telecommunications to science education, environmental research and disability studies. The foundation's Humanitarian City developed into a major rehabilitation and treatment complex, while its housing work extended across several Saudi regions. Together, these initiatives added an institutional humanitarian dimension to a public life more commonly associated with government and defence.
